title: India Eye 2-0 Lead as Bowlers Face Christchurch Test in Second T20I
excerpt: After Thursday's record 226 chase at Hagley Oval, Santner's fitness and India's one-spinner gamble dominate the build-up to Saturday's second T20I against New Zealand.
body:
• India lead the five-match T20I series 1-0 after chasing a record 226 to beat New Zealand by four wickets at Hagley Oval on Thursday.
  • The second T20I is at the same venue in Christchurch on Saturday, October 24, starting 12:30 pm IST (8:00 pm local), live on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV.
  • New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner is a fitness watch after landing awkwardly on his head; Ishan Kishan's groin strain could open a place for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.
  • India conceded 225 for 4 with one specialist spinner in the opener — whether they add Kuldeep Yadav or Varun Chakaravarthy is the main selection question.

India and New Zealand return to Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Saturday for the second T20I, two days after India chased 226 with two balls to spare to take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series. The match starts at 12:30 pm IST, 8:00 pm local time, with the toss at 12:00 pm IST, according to the match preview details for the October 24 fixture.

New Zealand posted 225 for 4 in the opener, powered by Glenn Phillips' 82 not out off 40 balls. India replied with Sanju Samson's 67 off 33 and Naman Dhir's unbeaten 42 off 15, winning by four wickets. It was a record chase, and it leaves the pressure exactly where the series headline puts it: on the bowlers, at a batting-friendly ground, under lights.

Santner's neck, New Zealand's problem

Mitchell Santner landed awkwardly on his head going for a catch in the 13th over of India's chase and left the field, before returning to finish his spell. "A bit of a whiplash there, but yeah, it's okay," he said afterwards, in reporting by SportsAdda on the second T20I build-up. The NZ Herald reported the Black Caps still face an anxious wait on his fitness.

They need him. Santner took 2 for 39, bowling Samson and having Ishan Kishan caught, and Michael Bracewell took 2 for 37. Matt Henry, Adam Milne and Lockie Ferguson all went at more than 11 an over, and New Zealand bowled 16 wides as India reached 94 for 1 in the powerplay. "I guess we have to find a way of trying to slow them down," Santner said.

The hosts are already thin. Rachin Ravindra is out of the T20Is with a dislocated right shoulder, and Mark Chapman and Zak Foulkes were ruled out before the series. Bevon Jacobs made 31 off 16 on Thursday, adding 50 in 24 balls with Phillips.

"I guess we have to find a way of trying to slow them down."

— Mitchell Santner, New Zealand captain

India's bowling bet

India played one specialist spinner, Axar Patel, and left Kuldeep Yadav and Varun Chakaravarthy, back from a side strain, on the bench. Shivam Dube was left out for Nitish Kumar Reddy, and the batting ran so deep that Bhuvneshwar Kumar was listed at No. 9. The cost was visible: five bowlers conceded 225, with Bhuvneshwar going for 49 in four overs without a wicket.

Dinesh Karthik, speaking on Cricbuzz, said he did not expect a change but would like one, arguing Bhuvneshwar could bat at No. 8 and free a place for a frontline spinner. Careerindia's preview listed India as likelier unchanged, with a probable XI of Abhishek Sharma, Samson, Kishan, Shreyas Iyer, Tilak Varma, Dhir, Axar, Reddy, Bhuvneshwar, Mayank Yadav and Arshdeep Singh.

One change may be forced. Reports from the camp linked Kishan's groin strain to a possible opportunity for 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who has waited through six T20Is on the bench. Samson's 67 and player-of-the-match award, built on a 93-run opening stand with Abhishek, make a voluntary change at the top hard to justify.

Pitch, conditions and what to watch

Fresh Hagley surfaces aid seam and swing early with even bounce, and dew can tilt the game toward chasing late. Saturday's outlook is clear and warm by day, easing to a cool, dry evening, with rain interruptions unlikely. Both previews expect the toss winner to bowl first, as Iyer did in the opener.

After Christchurch the series moves to Wellington on October 27, Auckland on October 30 and Hamilton on November 1. A win on Saturday puts India 2-0 up with three to play. For New Zealand, levelling at home is close to mandatory — and it starts with bowling a first six overs nothing like Thursday's.
